paras: The lynching near Mineral Wells, Mississippi, was the killing of an unnamed Black man, reported on 28 May 1919, after he was accused of attempting to attack a white woman on a country road. An alleged accomplice was arrested by the sheriff and moved for safekeeping, and the case is known only from a brief Memphis dispatch that the Richmond Planet printed under the headline "Another Lynching."

According to a dispatch dated Memphis, May 28, "meager reports" from Hernando and Olive Branch, Mississippi, told of the lynching that day near Mineral Wells of "a colored man." He was accused of holding up three white women who were riding in a buggy on a lonely road and of attempting to attack one of them. County officials, speaking by long-distance telephone, said he dragged the woman into a clump of bushes before the screams of her companions frightened him away.
The dispatch did not name the man or describe who killed him, how many took part, or how he died.

An alleged accomplice was said to have been arrested by the sheriff and a deputy and taken to Hernando, from where he was later removed to another village for safekeeping. No report of an inquest, arrests of lynchers, or the accomplice's fate appears in the coverage.

The Richmond Planet, a Black weekly, carried the Memphis dispatch twice in its 7 June 1919 issue, on pages 2 and 14, under the same headline, "Another Lynching." Both printings reproduced the wire text without comment, keeping its attribution of the accusation to county officials, and on page 2 the opening line was lost among advertising type. No other Black paper's report of the case appears in the coverage.

bases: The only report calls the killing of a colored man near Mineral Wells, Miss., a lynching, following an accusation of an attempted attack on a white woman (A2, A3).

The dispatch reports 'the lynching' of a colored man accused of attempting to attack a white woman, which states an extralegal killing on a crime pretext (A2, A3); it says nothing of who killed him, how many took part, or how, so the group element rests only on the word 'lynching'.
The event is known only from one Memphis dispatch, based on 'meager reports' from county officials by telephone, printed twice in the same issue of the Richmond Planet (A2, A3).
